quests.instruction: Touch the bag you carry on your back every single school day!
quests.question: Backpack
quests.hint: You wear this bag on your back with two straps over your shoulders.
quests.explanation: Well done! A backpack has room for books, pencils, and even a snack.
quests.funFact: Backpacks have two straps so the weight spreads evenly across both shoulders!

quests.instruction: Find the waxy stick that comes in every color of the rainbow!
quests.question: Crayon
quests.hint: It can melt if it gets too warm in the sun.
quests.explanation: That's right! We use crayons to fill our drawings with bright colors.
quests.funFact: Crayons are made from wax, which is why they melt in hot sunshine!

quests.instruction: Touch the tool with a handle and soft hairs used for painting!
quests.question: Paintbrush
quests.hint: After painting, it needs a good rinse in water to get clean.
quests.explanation: Well done! A paintbrush's soft bristles help spread color evenly.
quests.funFact: Paintbrush bristles can be made from soft animal hair or from nylon!

quests.instruction: Touch the tool we rub on paper before we press two pieces together!
quests.question: Glue Stick
quests.hint: You twist it up like a small tube before you rub it on paper.
quests.explanation: Well done! A glue stick helps our pictures and crafts hold together.
quests.funFact: Glue sticks were made so children could glue paper without sticky, messy fingers!

quests.instruction: Touch the word for the grown-up who stands at the front of class!
quests.question: Teacher
quests.hint: This person helps you learn new things and checks your work.
quests.explanation: Well done! A teacher guides the whole class through every lesson.
quests.funFact: Teachers often spend extra time planning fun lessons for their whole class!

quests.instruction: Find the item with a cover and many pages full of stories!
quests.question: Book
quests.hint: It can tell you a story about dragons, animals, or faraway places.
quests.explanation: That's right! We open a book and turn its pages to read.
quests.funFact: Some books have thousands of pages, while others have only a few!

quests.instruction: Touch the word for the room where you sit and learn each day!
quests.question: Classroom
quests.hint: This is the room where your desk and chair are found.
quests.explanation: Well done! A classroom is where students and teachers learn together every day.
quests.funFact: Classrooms around the world can look very different, but they are all places to learn!

quests.instruction: Touch the thin wooden tool that makes a mark when you write with it!
quests.question: Pencil
quests.hint: It leaves a soft grey line when it touches your page.
quests.explanation: Well done! A pencil makes marks that an eraser can rub away later.
quests.funFact: The soft grey part inside a pencil is called graphite, not lead at all!

quests.instruction: Touch the flat tool with numbers that helps us draw straight lines!
quests.question: Ruler
quests.hint: You press it flat on your paper before drawing a line.
quests.explanation: That's right! We use a ruler when we need a perfectly straight line.
quests.funFact: Long ago, people used their own feet and hands to measure things before rulers!

quests.instruction: Find the item we fill with our own writing and drawings!
quests.question: Notebook
quests.hint: You carry it to class to write down what your teacher says.
quests.explanation: That's right! We use a notebook to practice writing and take notes.
quests.funFact: Writing in a notebook every day is a great way to practice new words!

quests.instruction: Point to the tool teachers often use to write big words on a board!
quests.question: Marker
quests.hint: It has a cap you must remember to put back on.
quests.explanation: Yes! A marker draws bold, colorful lines on paper or a whiteboard.
quests.funFact: Some markers even smell like fruit, such as strawberry or grape!

quests.instruction: Point to the flat sheet we fold, cut, and draw on in class!
quests.question: Paper
quests.hint: It is thin, flat, and usually white or another light color.
quests.explanation: Yes! Paper is the flat sheet we write, draw, and color on.
quests.funFact: Most paper today is made from trees that are grown just for that purpose!

quests.instruction: Point to the word for the room filled with students and desks!
quests.question: Classroom
quests.hint: This room has desks, chairs, and a board at the front.
quests.explanation: Yes! A classroom is the room where you learn together with your teacher.
quests.funFact: Some classrooms have cozy reading corners with soft cushions for story time!

quests.instruction: Touch the furniture we pull up to the table before we sit down!
quests.question: Chair
quests.hint: It usually has four legs, a seat, and a back to lean on.
quests.explanation: Well done! A chair gives every student a comfy place to sit.
quests.funFact: Chairs have been used by people for thousands of years, even in ancient times!

quests.instruction: Point to the person who answers your questions and checks your work!
quests.question: Teacher
quests.hint: This person stands at the front of the classroom most of the day.
quests.explanation: Yes! A teacher is the person who helps students learn every day.
quests.funFact: A single teacher can help hundreds of students learn over many years!

quests.instruction: Touch the tool you press and rub when you write the wrong letter!
quests.question: Eraser
quests.hint: Pencils often carry a tiny piece of it on their top end.
quests.explanation: Correct! An eraser is a student's best friend when a letter looks wrong.
quests.funFact: Before rubber erasers, people used soft bread to rub out pencil marks!

quests.instruction: Point to the tool that helps our art projects stay stuck in place!
quests.question: Glue Stick
quests.hint: It feels a little bit sticky after you rub it on your page.
quests.explanation: Correct! A glue stick is perfect for sticking paper without any mess.
quests.funFact: A glue stick dries clear, so you can barely see it on your paper!

quests.instruction: Touch the item we open to read words and look at pictures!
quests.question: Book
quests.hint: It has a cover, and inside are many pages full of words.
quests.explanation: Well done! A book can teach us new things or tell a fun story.
quests.funFact: The very first books were written by hand, long before printing was invented!

quests.instruction: Point to the bag we pack with pencils, books, and snacks each morning!
quests.question: Backpack
quests.hint: It has zippers and pockets to keep your school things safe inside.
quests.explanation: Correct! A backpack keeps our school things together in one safe place.
quests.funFact: Some backpacks have a special pocket just the right size for a water bottle!

quests.instruction: Find the long, flat tool we use to measure how big something is!
quests.question: Ruler
quests.hint: It can tell you how many centimeters long your pencil is.
quests.explanation: Well done! A ruler has numbers that show us the length of things.
quests.funFact: Rulers can measure in centimeters on one side and inches on the other!

quests.instruction: Point to the box we carry to school full of yummy food!
quests.question: Lunchbox
quests.hint: You open it at lunchtime to find your sandwich or snack inside.
quests.explanation: Yes! A lunchbox carries our food safely to school until it's time to eat.
quests.funFact: Packing your own lunchbox can be a fun way to choose your favorite foods!

quests.instruction: Touch the bag that lives inside our backpack, full of writing tools!
quests.question: Pencil Case
quests.hint: It usually has a zipper to keep everything safely inside.
quests.explanation: Well done! A pencil case keeps our desk neat and organized.
quests.funFact: Some pencil cases can stand up on their own like a little box!

quests.instruction: Touch the tool we always use carefully to cut along a line!
quests.question: Scissors
quests.hint: It has two blades that open and close like a little mouth.
quests.explanation: Well done! Scissors help us cut paper into new shapes for our projects.
quests.funFact: The very first scissors were shaped very differently from the ones we use today!

quests.instruction: Touch the tool we use to color a picture, not to write words!
quests.question: Crayon
quests.hint: It feels waxy and comes in a big box of many bright colors.
quests.explanation: Well done! Crayons come in many colors so every picture can look different.
quests.funFact: One box of crayons can have more than sixty different colors inside!

quests.instruction: Point to the tool an artist uses to paint a colorful picture!
quests.question: Paintbrush
quests.hint: It has a long handle and soft bristles on one end.
quests.explanation: Yes! A paintbrush spreads paint smoothly across our paper.
quests.funFact: Artists use paintbrushes in many sizes, from tiny tips to big, wide ones!

quests.instruction: Point to the item that keeps your homework neat inside your backpack!
quests.question: Folder
quests.hint: It opens and closes like a thin book made of paper or plastic.
quests.explanation: Yes! A folder holds loose papers safely so they do not get lost or bent.
quests.funFact: Colorful folders can help students quickly find the right subject for each class!

quests.instruction: Touch the table where your pencils and notebook sit during class!
quests.question: Desk
quests.hint: It is flat on top, just the right size to hold your books.
quests.explanation: Well done! A desk gives every student their own space to work.
quests.funFact: Some classrooms use desks that can be pushed together to make small groups!

quests.instruction: Point to the word that describes you when you are sitting in class!
quests.question: Student
quests.hint: This person carries a backpack and sits at a desk to learn.
quests.explanation: Yes! A student is a person who goes to school to learn new things.
quests.funFact: Being a good student means trying your best, even when something feels hard!

quests.instruction: Find the tool you hold to draw a picture of your family!
quests.question: Pencil
quests.hint: You need to sharpen its tip so it can write again.
quests.explanation: Correct! Every student uses a pencil to practice writing every day.
quests.funFact: Long ago, people wrote with sticks and feathers before pencils were invented!

quests.instruction: Touch the item with pages that are empty until we write in them!
quests.question: Notebook
quests.hint: Its pages start out empty until you fill them with your writing.
quests.explanation: Well done! A notebook is where your own writing and drawings live.
quests.funFact: Some notebooks have a spiral of wire so the pages can turn easily!
